Codex review: blocked before merge. _Reviewed September 13, 2026, 1:35 AM ET / 05:35 UTC (Revision 3)._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes The PR snapshots registered OpenClaw and declared plugin databases while copying other SQLite files and sidecars unchanged, reporting warnings, and skipping unresolvable foreign SQLite links. ## Merge readiness ⛔ **Blocked before merge - 4 items remain** This remains a useful fix for a current backup failure. No blocking code defect was found, but the previously identified archive-reader compatibility decision remains unresolved. **Priority:** P2 **Reviewed head:** `bf81b138f9482db6b7c76c08bbcd93581ac2daa7` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | A coherent fix with relevant real CLI evidence and meaningful regression coverage; compatibility acceptance remains a separate merge gate. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | Sufficient (live_output): Retained PR-body observations cover real CLI create, verify, and restore, byte preservation, managed refusal, WAL hardlinks, and concurrent writes through the changed backup owner; the latest formatter relocation does not invalidate that evidence. | | **Patch quality** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (live_output): Retained PR-body observations cover real CLI create, verify, and restore, byte preservation, managed refusal, WAL hardlinks, and concurrent writes through the changed backup owner; the latest formatter relocation does not invalidate that evidence. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 9 items | Current main still has the reported failure mechanism: Fetched main classifies included SQLite files under state and configured agent roots as snapshot candidates without requiring declared ownership. They still reach verified snapshot creation, so the central change remains necessary.
Ownership and archive handling: Creation reads agent registrations from the online root snapshot, seals the ownership inventory, retains managed database validation, and records opaque-file warnings. Verification derives agent ownership from the archived registry.
Shipped reader incompatibility: The v2026.9.4 verifier rejects SQLite sidecars under state and agent roots. Consequently, archives containing the newly permitted opaque sidecars cannot be verified or restored by that release. | | **Findings** | None | None. | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together OpenClaw’s archive backup combines configuration, state, credentials, and workspaces into a recovery archive. Database ownership determines which files receive consistent SQLite snapshots and which checks verification performs before restore. ```mermaid flowchart TD A[Configuration and plugin declarations] --> B[Backup resource plan] C[Root database snapshot] --> D[Captured agent registry] B --> E[Database ownership decision] D --> E E --> F[Managed snapshots or opaque files] F --> G[Recovery archive] G --> H[Verify and restore] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should this change require a newer archive reader and make plugin snapshot guarantees depend on explicit backupResources declarations? | **Accept and document the new recovery contract:** Retain the ownership-based behavior, document the required reader, and record old-reader rejection alongside successful candidate restoration. | Why: The implementation changes shipped recovery and plugin backup guarantees even though the numeric archive schema and manifest fields remain unchanged. ## Before merge - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Archives containing opaque SQLite sidecars will fail verification and restore on v2026.9.4; the supported reader requirement remains undocumented and unaccepted. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Undeclared plugin databases lose automatic consistent snapshots and deleted-page removal. Existing installations need an explicit compatibility policy for this changed meaning of backupResources. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - Record maintainer acceptance of the changed backup guarantees, document the supported reader requirement, and retain old/new reader compatibility evidence. - [ ] **Resolve maintainer decision** - Resolve the maintainer decision shown above before merge.

Members: - `canonical`: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/144552 - The open report supplies the concrete reproduction and is explicitly linked by this PR. Proposal only: this assessment does not dispatch repair, suppress jobs, mutate sibling items, close, or merge anything. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Accept a documented reader requirement (recommended)** Approve the changed guarantees with explicit recovery documentation and an old/new reader compatibility record. 2. **Preserve the existing recovery contract** Revise the exception before merge if older readers or implicit plugin snapshot guarantees must remain supported. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep a single captured ownership inventory and make the accepted reader requirements and plugin snapshot guarantees explicit in recovery guidance. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes. The foreign-key fixture reaches unconditional snapshot validation on fetched main, and the PR records a real CLI failure; this review did not execute it. Is this the best way to solve the issue? Yes, the shared ownership decision addresses the reported failure without globally weakening managed database checks; acceptance still depends on the changed recovery contract. Consequently, archives containing the newly permitted opaque sidecars cannot be verified or restored by that release. ([`src/commands/backup-verify.ts:302`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107/src/commands/backup-verify.ts#L302), [3a9d69db306c](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/3a9d69db306cd7f081e06254cb89c4bcc14a7107)) - **Documented guarantee change:** The updated documentation explicitly removes live consistency and deleted-data-removal guarantees for undeclared SQLite files. Existing plugin include declarations now select managed snapshots; the documentation does not identify the incompatible older archive reader. Public docs: [`docs/cli/backup.md`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/backup). ([`docs/cli/backup.md:350`](https://docs.openclaw.ai/cli/backup), [bf81b138f948](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf81b138f9482db6b7c76c08bbcd93581ac2daa7)) - **Re-review continuity:** Comparison with the previous reviewed head shows no changes to capture, verification, or compatibility documentation. GitHub’s exact-head commit patch confirms that the latest commit only relocates summary formatting and updates its imports. The earlier cyclic-link concern is addressed by explicit skip-and-warning handling. ([`src/commands/backup-summary.ts:3`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/bf81b138f9482db6b7c76c08bbcd93581ac2daa7/src/commands/backup-summary.ts#L3), [bf81b138f948](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/bf81b138f9482db6b7c76c08bbcd93581ac2daa7)) - **Retained real CLI evidence:** The supplied complete PR body, captured under sourceRevision 49f5242d3afc6740c57f88059f4ffd3e7a1fac338fc96341ac068cfdfa8ff3bd, reports baseline failure, candidate create/verify/restore preserving seven foreign files and sidecars, managed refusal controls, WAL-aware hardlinks, and successful capture during 10 ms commits with 309 rows during a 3.6-second run. These observations cover the changed production path; they were not independently rerun during this read-only review. (role: unverified routing candidate; confidence: low) - **steipete:** Suggested for follow-up; no historical authorship or introduction is verified. (role: unverified routing candidate; confidence: low) ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Document and record old/new reader compatibility, including v2026.9.4 rejection of opaque sidecars and successful candidate restoration. ### Rating scale | Score | Internal tier | Crab rank | Meaning | |---:|:---:|---|---| | **6/6** | S | 🦀 challenger crab | Exceptional readiness | | **5/6** | A | 🦞 diamond lobster | Very strong readiness | | **4/6** | B | 🐚 platinum hermit | Good normal PR; ordinary maintainer review | | **3/6** | C | 🦐 gold shrimp | Useful, but confidence is limited | | **2/6** | D | 🦪 silver shellfish | Proof or implementation needs work | | **1/6** | F | 🧂 unranked krab | Not merge-ready | | N/A | NA | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Rating does not apply | Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality.
